subject: Lumenix mid-contract uplift and synchronized renewal path
body:
From: Sarah Owens <sarah.owens@lumenix.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumenix AP <ap@lumenix.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract uplift — options to align renewal (Oct 15)

Hi Neha,

We had a spike in production usage over the past 6 weeks and expect sustained higher consumption going into Q4. Procurement asked me to reach out about options for adding committed capacity now and aligning our contract renewal to our fiscal year (Oct 15).

Quick context: current commit: 1.2T tokens/year (annualized). Expected uplift: additional 450M tokens/year starting May 1.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can we add the uplift mid-contract and have billing smoothed across the remainder of the contract?
- What discounts apply for a partial-year uplift vs. annualizing and co-terming?
- Procurement prefers a single PO and quarterly invoicing if we can make the numbers work.

Attached a draft PO and rough usage forecast for your finance team to review.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Owens
Sr. Procurement Manager | Lumenix

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Owens <sarah.owens@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — options to align renewal (Oct 15)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear context and the PO draft. We can definitely support an uplift and a synchronized renewal; below are three practical paths with trade-offs. I copied Ben (pricing) to seed numbers once you confirm which approach you prefer.

1) Staged top-up (no change to co-term) — simplest for procurement
   - Add a mid-contract top-up for the 450M tokens starting May 1.
   - Charge pro-rata for the remaining contract months (May 1 — Oct 15) then normalize on the next renewal.
   - No discount on the pro-rated portion; full-year pricing applies at next annual renewal.

2) Voucher + bridge credit — smooths invoicing and reduces near-term sticker shock
   - Redwood issues a voucher equal to X% of invoice (applied as credit) to spread cost.
   - Procurement can submit one PO for the full uplift; we invoice quarterly and apply voucher credits each quarter.
   - Slightly lower near-term cash for Lumenix; discount impact is limited (voucher is not a permanent discount).

3) Annualize & co-term (preferred for larger commitments)
   - Convert uplift to an annualized commitment effective immediately, with a pro-rated charge for the partial first year, then co-term to Oct 15 by annualizing the entire commit.
   - Apply a blended uplift discount tier based on total commit band (e.g., +450M moves you into the 1.6T band for tiered pricing).
   - Requires contract amendment to co-term; offers the best per-token economics.

If your priority is single PO + quarterly invoicing, Option 2 (Voucher + bridge credit) or Option 3 (Annualize & co-term) will work — Option 2 is faster to close, Option 3 gives better unit economics.

Next steps: if you can confirm preferred path and whether AP needs line-item pricing on the PO, Ben will draft a quote and I can provide a short amendment template for legal/PO.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Owens <sarah.owens@lumenix.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — options to align renewal (Oct 15)

Hi Sarah / Neha — high level numbers below (rounding for clarity). Happy to run a more granular model if you share the current invoice and expected monthly ramp.

Assumptions: current commit = 1.2T tokens/year; uplift = +450M tokens/year (effective 5/1); current renewal target Oct 15.

Option A — Staged top-up (pro-rata):
 - Pro-rata for May 1 — Oct 15 (5.5 months) on 450M = charge for ~206M tokens this period at list rate
 - Effective blended unit cost = list price (no uplift discount)

Option B — Voucher + quarterly billing:
 - Full uplift accepted on PO for 450M annualized; we invoice quarterly based on usage; Redwood issues a 6% voucher credit applied across invoices for the next 4 quarters as a smoothing mechanism
 - Net near-term cash reduced, final effective discount ~6% first year only

Option C — Annualize & co-term (recommended for economics):
 - Annualize 450M immediately; convert total commit to 1.65T and co-term to Oct 15 via amendment
 - Blended uplift discount: 3% on the existing band plus incremental 7% on the additional band — overall blended uplift ~5%
 - Requires signature on amendment; legal lead time typically 3–5 business days

Attachment: Lumenix_uplift_quote_v1.pdf (pricing table, stub)

If you want me to produce an invoice schedule aligning with a single PO + quarterly invoicing (Option B), say the word and I’ll add exact line-item amounts and the voucher credit schedule.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Pricing & Deals | Redwood Inference

Neha / Ben — thanks for the quick options and the quote stub. Procurement preference: single PO that covers the uplift (we can do the total uplift annualized on PO), quarterly invoicing to match our internal cadence, and a smoothing credit is helpful.

Two asks before we move:
1) Can the voucher credit be structured as a "prepaid credit" on our ledger (so it shows as a line on the PO)? Finance prefers to see credits documented against the PO.
2) If we annualize and co-term, we need exact line items for the PO (annual total, quarterly invoicing amounts, and the first pro-rated invoice amount).

I've attached an updated PO template with our AP coding. If you can provide a version that maps to Option B and Option C line items, I can route internally and aim to sign the PO next week.

Sarah

- Provide a DocuSign link for whichever path Lumenix prefers; legal sign-off for the amendment is typically quick for this size.

If we proceed with Option B, we'll document the voucher as a prepaid credit line on the PO and itemize the quarterly invoice amounts plus the credit schedule. If Option C is selected, the first invoice will be a pro-rated charge (May 1–Oct 15) and then quarterly invoices thereafter.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon (May 3): Ben shares PO-ready line items and a sample invoice schedule
- Tue (May 4): I send the amendment + DocuSign and we aim to have PO signed by end of next week

Sarah — does that timeline work on your side?

Best,
